storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form cx:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the cx:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference; distinct from cx:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Realm-scoped pseudonymous credential reference; validated by the E2EE profile. v1 core uses Realm as the boundary; Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as a content-addressed canonical Anchor hash.
Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.
Store the scope string as an opaque deployment-level identifier; it appears in server describe, Realm policy, and high-risk proof transcripts.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk proofs (e.g. cx.cross_signing.reset §14.1). NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

id_kinds.description: Moderation appeal ID — opaque key for the cx.component.moderation_appeal.v1 cell. Created by cx.moderation.appeal.submit; referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.

Agent protocol session ID. Note the cross-surface naming: this typed ID uses the short form `agent_session`, while the corresponding event kinds use the full form `cx.agent.protocol_session.{start,status,result}` and capability actions use `cx.agent.session.{start,cancel,stream_status,attach_artifact,read_transcript}` (frozen wire_compat_grandfather bridge — see capabilities.md §5.0 and renames.json migration_group `wire_compat_grandfather`). The three surfaces all refer to the same session concept; downstream tooling MUST NOT assume `cx:<event-prefix>:<uuid>` mechanical derivation.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_class). A pair MAY have multiple series during rotation or migration; the active series is selected by the signed active-series record, not by server return order. Used by cx.schema.key_backup.v1.series_id and recovery flows to detect rollback. See identity/key-management.md §7.6.
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form

SFU-local participant handle (CXP-0010). Scope limited to `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`; derived from `(realm_id, call_id, focus_id, device_id, issuer_service_did, issued_at_bucket)` by the media service token issuer. MUST NOT carry any actor-identifying material; only appears in `cx.call.state.participants[].participant_identity` and in `participant_binding`. The wire value MUST use the canonical UUIDv7-shaped `cx:rtc_participant:<uuid>` form; implementations MAY derive the random bits from the media-service token input, but the version and variant nibbles MUST satisfy the UUIDv7 pattern.
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use cx:grant:<uuid>.

Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. See zh/models/circle.md.
Signed capability grant object ID used by cx.schema.capability.v1 and grant/revoke references.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery flow. Referenced by cx.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by §15 recovery proofs. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.
